title: Abortion and the Unborn
lead: What the Bible says about life before birth, and how Jews and the early church came to forbid abortion and the killing of newborns, which some Greek thinkers accepted.

sections.h: Life in the womb in the Bible
sections.b: The Bible has no law that names abortion. It speaks often of God's care for life before birth: "you wove me together in my mother's womb" (Psalm 139:13); "Before I shaped you in the belly, I knew you" (Jeremiah 1:5); John the Baptist leaps in Elizabeth's womb (Luke 1:41-44). The law of Exodus 21:22-25, about a pregnant woman struck in a brawl, is read in different ways: either her children are born early and live, with the penalty of "life for life" for harm to mother or child, or she miscarries and the penalty is a fine, with harm to her alone punished in kind. The site's notes on Exodus 21 give the readings, and the card at Jeremiah 1 gives how churches use Jeremiah 1:5.

Some Greek thinkers accepted both practices. Aristotle proposed a law "that no deformed child shall be reared," and that a child conceived against the city's rules be aborted "before it has developed sensation and life" (Politics 7, 1335b, Rackham's translation). Josephus says the Law "enjoins us to bring up all our offspring, and forbids women to cause abortion of what is begotten" (Against Apion 2.202, Whiston's translation). Jewish sources do not all read the Law the same way: Exodus 21:22-23 sets a fine when a struck woman's children "come out" and no harm follows, and the Greek Septuagint makes it a different law, a fine if the child was not yet "formed" (exeikonismenon) and life for life if it was (see the notes at Exodus 21:22). The Two Ways of the Didache and Barnabas forbids both: "You must not murder a child by abortion, and you must not kill one that has been born" (Didache 2:2; Barnabas 19:5), and lists among the ways of death "murderers of children and destroyers of what God has formed" (Didache 5:2). R. A. Kraft notes that the first line means abortion, "apparently before birth since infanticide is next mentioned."
